newsitem.title: USA: Indonesia 96/97 palm oil exports up -- US attache.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia 96/97 palm oil exports up -- US attache.

text.p: Indonesia will export nearly 2.2 million tonnes of palm oil in 1996/97, a 20 percent gain from the previous year, the U.S. agriculture attache in Jakarta forecast in a report released Wednesday.
The export forecast of 2.19 million tonnes was slightly higher than an earlier estimate of 2.1 million tonnes. Exports in 1995-96, which ended last September 30, were 1.812 million.
"Palm oil exports for (marketing year) 1996/97, are now forecast to reach approximately 2.2 million tonnes, boasting a 20-percent increase from the previous marketing year," the attache wrote.
"However, due to the export tax system, this growth will only occur if production expansion remains on track and reaches 4.95-5.0 million tonnes."
Production was forecast at 4.95 million tonnes, up sharply from last year's 4.5 million tonnes and the earlier estimate of 4.65 million tonnes.
"The increase is due to a larger harvested area as more trees planted two-and-a-half to three years ago have started bearing fruit," the report said.
About 1.4 million hectares of trees were expected to be harvested in 1996/97, compared to 1.22 million last year.
Planted area has expanded to 2.2 million hectares.

"Now the Government of Indonesia has set their production target (approximately 8.5 million tonnes) so that Indonesia will become the largest palm oil producer in the world by 2003, surpassing Malaysia," the attache wrote. "Strong growth will continue in palm oil production because of increased planting and because about 50 percent of the plantations consist of new plantations."
Palm meal exports were pegged at 680,000 tonnes in 1996/97, compared to 602,000 tonnes in 1995/96. No palm kernel exports were forecast.
